messages.content: Predict a real adult's choice in a binary Dictator Game involving GiveDirectly, a charity providing direct cash transfers to low-income households in sub-Saharan Africa. The request gives two complete allocations of experimental tokens: tokens kept by the participant and tokens sent to the charity. The participant must choose one whole option; the components cannot be mixed and the totals need not be equal across options. One token converts to one US cent ($0.01). The charity is a passive recipient with no acceptance or return decision. There are 24 tasks in a randomized order. The participant has 10 seconds per task. If no choice is made within that limit, both the participant and charity receive nothing if that task is selected for payment. At the end, one task is randomly selected and only that task is paid according to the participant's decision; do not add allocations across tasks as actual earnings. The charity was illustrated by Beatrice, age 31, and her two young children living in Kenya; the participant was shown their photograph. The photograph and exact preceding article wording are not supplied in this request. Earlier choices, when supplied, are prior decisions, not realized payments. Predict the allocation the participant selects within the decision limit, without advice or moral evaluation. Reply only with compact JSON in this key order: {"self_tokens":integer,"charity_tokens":integer}. It must equal one of the two offered complete options.

The participant is an adult recruited from US Amazon Mechanical Turk. Before the decisions the participant read a one-page NewScientist article presenting neurological evidence in support of the claim that humans do not have free will. They could advance only after at least one minute and were asked for a one- or two-sentence summary, with payment potentially affected if they did not provide it. The study was introduced as being about text exposure and happiness.
Current decision position: 1 of 24. Option A: keep 60 tokens, give 60 to charity. Option B: keep 0 tokens, give 100 to charity. Predict the selected complete allocation.
Own background: recorded gender male; reported religious affiliation: no religious affiliation. Before reading the article, own happiness rating was 5; after reading and before any allocation it was 5 (recorded rating scale maximum 10).
